title: The Intimate Interrupter
coreMove: Distraction loosens when you stop treating discomfort as a stop sign, name the escape sensation, and keep acting while boredom, fear, or impatience is present.

exampleSpecs.audience: Thanh, a researcher revising a grant section
exampleSpecs.stakes: A weak paragraph could delay a project he cares about.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Shinzen Young's icy-water lesson to separate sensation from resistance.

exampleSpecs.audience: Beckett, an editor stuck on a script bridge
exampleSpecs.stakes: A release deadline could turn into another night of avoidance.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Mary Oliver's intimate interrupter sounding friendly rather than hostile.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jean, a student finishing a thesis and tax packet
exampleSpecs.stakes: Avoidance could make both an ordinary duty and a cherished goal worse.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Gregg Krech to show reluctance toward both chores and meaningful work.

exampleSpecs.audience: Taras, an architect postponing a public model
exampleSpecs.stakes: The ideal proposal may die untouched if it never enters public time.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the Shiraz architect's refusal as fear of finite reality.

exampleSpecs.audience: Yves, a consultant reviewing his own escape pattern
exampleSpecs.stakes: A useful client judgment could be replaced by harmless-looking busywork.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat social media relief as evidence of the sensation being avoided.

exampleSpecs.audience: Cyrille, a teacher rebuilding tomorrow's class opener
exampleSpecs.stakes: A weak opener will make the next day's lesson drift.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show freedom growing when the impulse to flee is felt without being obeyed.
